name: grip-sudoku
description: Sudoku SPA built as a GRIP demo: no React state, everything is a grip

paragraphs: A complete Sudoku single-page app — sign in, pick a difficulty, play with pen and pencil marks, undo/redo, a timer, mistake limits, auto-save, a dashboard with stats and leaderboards, and a profile with run history — built as a demonstration of GRIP (@owebeeone/grip-react).

The point of the demo: there is no React state in this app. Not one useState, useEffect, useRef, useReducer, useMemo, useCallback, or useLayoutEffect. Every value a component renders is read from a grip, and every change goes through a tap. That rule is enforced by a lint rule and an independent test (see Enforcement), so it can't quietly erode.

Sign in with demo@gripsudoku.app and any password. The backend is mocked — auth, stats, and leaderboards are fixture data served through taps with a simulated network delay, so the UI exercises real loading/async paths.
